summary: Specifies an application-level protocol called the Remote User Telnet service. Any host implementing this service must follow the protocol. This RFC is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 818 specifies a Remote User Telnet service for hosts that choose to provide it. A user connects to port 107 and uses the Telnet Protocol on that connection.

questions: what is the remote user telnet service
subtitle: A well-known Telnet port for remote user access to hosts without a system executive.

tldr.problem: Some small hosts have limited functionality and no system executive for a remote user to access through Server Telnet.
tldr.mechanism: The memo specifies that a host choosing to provide the Remote User Telnet service accepts User Telnet connections on port 107 and uses the Telnet Protocol.
tldr.outcome: This RFC is marked Historic and records the service specification and a BBN terminal-concentrator example.

today: RFC 818 is marked Historic. It specifies the Remote User Telnet service for hosts that choose to provide it.

sections.title: Remote User Telnet
sections.content:
Most Server Telnet services connect a user to a system executive, such as TOPS20 EXEC or the Unix Shell. Some small hosts may have limited functionality and no executive.

For hosts choosing to provide the Remote User Telnet service, the RFC designates port 107, also written as 153 octal, and specifies use of the Telnet Protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The service is for a host that offers remote terminal access without a general system executive. A user connects to the specified port and communicates with Telnet.

sections.title: Using the Service
sections.content:
A user opens a connection to port 107 on the host. The originating user then uses Telnet on that connection to communicate with the server.

The RFC makes provision of the service optional: it applies on hosts that choose to offer it.
sections.plainLanguage: The client connects to the service port and runs the Telnet protocol over the connection. The host decides whether to offer the service.

sections.title: BBN TC68K Example
sections.content:
The RFC describes a BBN TC68K terminal concentrator with one network connection and sixteen RS232 terminal connections. Its software used IP, ICMP, TCP, and Telnet.

For remote testing, the TC68K could put a user Telnet back to back with a server Telnet through a Pseudo Teletype device driver. The operator then appeared to be using a terminal local to the remote unit.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN used the service to connect an operator to a remote terminal concentrator for testing. A Pseudo Teletype device passed a character stream between the two Telnet processes.
